entries.title: How can a fire change which plants grow in a forest?
entries.answer: Fire may harm trees and animals, but some ecosystems developed with fires from time to time. In some forests, fires remove low plants that compete for sunlight. Heat can open some kinds of tightly closed cones, releasing seeds. Plants may also sprout again from roots that survived below ground. An unusually severe fire can leave very different effects than a mild one, so what grows back depends on the place and the fire.
facts: Scientists compare plants before and after fires to learn how a forest changes.

entries.title: How can a pile of oysters become a reef again?
entries.answer: An oyster can attach to a hard object. If many oysters grow next to and on top of one another, their shells form a rough structure with cracks and ledges. Small animals can hide there. Oysters also filter tiny pieces of food from water as they feed. Where older reefs have disappeared, groups can restore them by providing clean shells or another firm base for young oysters to attach to and grow.
facts: Fish and crabs can find food around a reef made of oysters.

entries.title: How can an animal return to a place where it disappeared?
entries.answer: A species may disappear from one place while still living somewhere else. Reintroduction means bringing some back to a suitable place in its former range. Before releasing animals, teams study threats, food, shelter, and other wildlife already there. A very rare species may need young raised in a protected setting. After release, people check whether the animals survive, find food, and have young. The hope is for a wild group that can continue on its own.
facts: Black-footed ferrets returned to some parts of the American prairie through reintroduction.

entries.title: What does it mean when a species is endangered?
entries.answer: An endangered species is one that is in danger of disappearing. If the last living member is gone, the species is extinct. A species can be in trouble because it has little habitat left, because there are too few young growing up, or because changing conditions make it harder to find food. Scientists look at where a species lives, how many are there, and whether groups are getting smaller. Those clues can help people decide how to protect it.
facts: A kind of animal can disappear from one region and still be alive somewhere else.

entries.title: When does a new plant or animal become invasive?
entries.answer: Some living things reach new places when people carry boats, plants, soil, or other goods between regions. Some newcomers never establish a wild population. Some live in their new place without harming it. One is considered invasive if it spreads outside its native range and causes harm. For example, a fast-growing plant could crowd out other plants that local insects need. A new animal might eat food that another species depends on. Scientists look for actual harm, rather than judging a kind of life just because it came from somewhere else.
facts: A species can cause problems in one area and be useful in its native habitat.

entries.title: Why did wolves return to Yellowstone?
entries.answer: Gray wolves once lived in Yellowstone, but people removed them from the park and few remained nearby. In the 1990s, wildlife workers brought wolves from Canada back to the area. Wolves can hunt animals such as elk, which in turn feed on leaves and other plants. Animals can act differently when a predator returns. Scientists still compare the effects of wolves with other changes, including weather, food, and the actions of people.
facts: Wolves were released into Yellowstone in 1995 and 1996.

entries.title: Why do monarch butterflies fly south in autumn?
entries.answer: Many monarchs from eastern parts of North America head south in autumn. They gather in cool mountain forests in central Mexico, where the winter usually lets them survive without laying many eggs. When weather warms, they fly north and begin laying eggs. Later generations continue the journey. A female monarch looks for milkweed for its young, because monarch caterpillars eat milkweed leaves. Adult butterflies visit flowers for nectar and can use many different kinds.
facts: The fall travelers live longer than many monarchs born in summer.

entries.title: Why would people build a bridge for animals?
entries.answer: A road can cut between places where animals eat, drink, or raise young. A bridge covered with soil and plants can let some animals cross above moving cars. Others use a passage below the pavement. Fences can keep animals from trying to enter the road and guide them to a crossing. People choose locations by finding existing animal travel routes. A crossing can help keep part of a larger habitat connected.
facts: Different animals use different sizes and kinds of passage.
